Summation operator


Definition
 If {xi : i = 1, . . . , n} denotes a sequence of n numbers, then we write the sum of
these numbers as

        ∑n
                               xi = x1 + x2 + · · · + xn
                           i=1


Properties

For any constant c, we have

          ∑n
                                       c = nc                                (1)

                                   i=1

Conditional expectation, Conditional variance

Conditional expectation


 If there are two random variables X, Y , the expectation E(Y ) is a single value,
but the conditional expectation E(Y |X) is a function of X.

Properties of conditional expectation

    1  For any function c(X),

                            E[c(X)|X] = c(X)                          (6)

    2  For functions a(X) and b(X),

                E[a(X)Y + b(X)|X] = a(X)E[Y |X] + b(X)             (7)

    3 The law of iterated expectations: for any random variables X, Y

                         E[E(Y |X)] = E[Y ]                         (8)

    4   If X and Y are independent, then E(Y |X) = E(Y ).

Conditional expectation, Conditional variance

Conditional variance





Definition
Given random variables X and Y , the variance of Y , conditional on X is defined
as

                     Var(Y |X) = E(Y 2|X) −E(Y |X)2                    (9)


Properties

 If X and Y are independent, then

                           Var(Y |X) = Var(Y )

Independence, Mean independence, Uncorrelatedness

Independence




Definition
The random variables X, Y are independent random variables if and only if their
joint cumulative distribution function (cdf) is the product of the marginal cdfs for
any (X, Y ), ie

                       FX,Y (x, y) = FX(x)FY (y)


Properties

Suppose random variables X, Y are independent, the following statements are
true:
    1 E(Y |X) = E(Y )

    2 E(XY ) = E(X)E(Y )

Independence, Mean independence, Uncorrelatedness

Mean independence (Zero conditional mean)





Definition
A random variable Y  is said to mean independent of X  if and only if

                       E(Y |X) = E(Y )





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                              September 14, 2024          12 / 18

Independence, Mean independence, Uncorrelatedness

Uncorrelatedness (Zero correlation)





Definition
A random variable Y  is said to be uncorrelated with X  if and only if

                      Cov(X, Y ) = 0, or ρXY = 0





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                              September 14, 2024          13 / 18

Independence, Mean independence, Uncorrelatedness

Relationship





By the definitions, we can show
     Independence ⇒mean independence ⇒uncorrelatedness (prove: in class)
     Independence ⇍mean independence ⇍uncorrelatedness (prove: in class)
Therefore, the independence assumption is stronger than mean independence,
and mean independence is stronger than uncorrelatedness.

SLR.1 Linear in Parameters

SLR.2 Random Sampling

We have a random sample of size n, {(Xi, Yi) : i = 1, 2, . . . , n}.

Note: random sample here means that {(Xi, Yi)} are independent and identically
distributed (iid) sequence of random variables.

Review of SLR.1-4

Review of SLR.1-4



SLR.3 Sample Variation in the Explanatory Variable

The sample outcomes on X, namely, {(Xi) : i = 1, 2, . . . , n}, are not all the same
value.


SLR.4 Zero Conditional Mean
The error u has an expected value of zero given any value of the explanatory
variable. In other words,

                           E(u|X) = 0

Note: SLR.4 implies
    E(u) = 0 (by the law of iterated expectation)
    Cov(X, u) = 0 (but not vice versa !)
